rationale:
Closes s327-A4-g5v-03-01's signed ESCALATE per its own reopenCondition: "Reopen when a new figures.tsx component exists depicting a rectangular block with a rectangular notch removed (subtractive, not additive, unit-cube register, no circles/pricing) so it can be attached to c1 and/or c2; or if remedials[0].concept.body is ever authored to diverge from c2.body." A4's finding (reports/closure/S327_ASSESS_A4.md#g5v-03-01), re-verified by reading the lesson JSON directly before touching anything: neither c1 nor c2 carried a figure key, and this lesson's defining action -- subtracting a notch from a full block -- was never visually or interactively represented anywhere (the two barBuilder widgets, i1 and i2, only ever build the pre-notch full block; the subtraction itself was narrated only in successFeedback text). A4 checked every plausibly-relevant registered figure and found none conforming: vm-l-shape and vm-add-volumes depict a DIFFERENT, additive decomposition (cut into two boxes and add) that contradicts this lesson's own subtractive method; sg-subtracting has the right abstract principle (outer minus removed) but the wrong concrete shape (a circle, not this Grade-5-rectangular-prisms-only course's rectangle) and the wrong register (pricing/manufacturing framing, not cube-counting). Nothing about the math, remedials, or progression was defective per A4 -- the whole finding was the visual/spatial gap, genuinely blocked on src/** figure authority.

FIX: authored a new figures.tsx component, VmNotchBlock (registered as "vm-notch-block"), depicting a full rectangular block with a rectangular notch cut from its top-right corner, drawn in this exact register: a light-filled SKY outer rectangle (the full block) with a white, dashed-BERRY-outlined rectangle at one corner (the notch, styled as "removed" following sg-subtracting's own outer-minus-removed convention, just corrected to rectangular/corner/unit-cube register instead of circular/center/pricing register) -- satisfying A4's reopenCondition exactly: subtractive not additive, rectangular not circular, no pricing framing. The figure's <title> states "Subtract the notch from the full block: 48 minus 15 equals 33 unit cubes remain" and its aria-label spells out the same claim in full sentences naming the dashed notch as now-empty space -- a genuine mathematical description, not a generic caption. Arithmetic verified: 48 - 15 = 33. These numbers are a fresh illustrative instance, deliberately distinct from every worked pair already authored in this lesson (i1: 5-by-6 block, notch 8, 30-8=22; i2: 4-by-7 block, notch 6, 28-6=22; k2: 6x4-16, 24-16=8; ch1: 4x9-24, 36-24=12; remedial: 4-by-7 block, notch 6, same as i2) -- confirmed by direct enumeration in src/components/s328Figures.test.tsx's own test ("matches no worked pair already in the lesson"). This matters because the figure is bound to BOTH c1 and c2: c1 sits immediately before i1's own predict-before-reveal question ("A 5-by-6 block with an 8-cube notch -- volume? 22 or 38"), so a figure using i1's own numbers there would hand away that answer before the learner commits to a prediction; because vm-notch-block's numbers (48/15/33) never appear anywhere else in the lesson, binding it to c1 illustrates the general method (full block, then subtract the notch) without previewing i1's, i2's, k2's, k3's, or ch1's own answers. c2 is a natural second binding of the same figure (c2's sentence -- "the subtraction happens once, on the whole solid" -- is the same idea restated, and reusing one correct figure across a lesson's two concept steps is an accepted, precedented pattern in this exact course: g5v-02-02 binds vm-base-height to both its c1 and c2). Also bound the same figure to remedials[0].concept (rem-g5v-composite-c), whose body is byte-identical to c2.body (a separately-documented, non-gating S316-section-6 debt item that A4 explicitly did not fix) -- since the figure already truthfully matches c2.body, it trivially and correctly matches the remedial concept's identical text too, and this mirrors Worker D's best-in-batch pattern from S316_ADJUDICATION_REMEDIAL_STANDARD.md section 4 ("attached a registered figure to 23/23 remedial concepts, always reusing one of the lesson's own verified c1/c2 figures").

visualDecision=SUFFICIENT (not merely PREFERRED): this lesson now has a correct, register-appropriate static figure on both concept steps PLUS genuine interactive/manipulable coverage of the same idea via the two barBuilder widgets (i1 builds the full block and its predict field forces a subtract-vs-add commitment; i2 builds a second full block whose successFeedback states the same subtraction) -- the same combination (static figure + real interactive widgets covering the core action) that earned g5v-01-01 a SUFFICIENT rating from this same A4 assessor in the same batch, and the exact visualDecision value this repo's own tooling uses for a figure-authority ESCALATE that has just been discharged (precedent: reports/closure/cowork-staging/laneA-s324-engfig.jsonl records s324-engfig-df3-01-01 and s324-engfig-df3-01-02, both KEEP/SUFFICIENT/FIT, for the structurally identical situation of a new parameterized figures.tsx component closing a signed figure-gap ESCALATE). decision=KEEP because A4 already confirmed every other axis defect-free and the sole blocking axis (visual) is now resolved -- matching this course's own established pattern (g5v-01-01, g5v-01-02, g5v-02-02 all carry decision KEEP alongside their own visualDecision ratings). gradeLanguageDecision=FIT is carried forward unchanged from A4 -- no body, narration, or widget text was touched, only a figure key was added to three steps.

rationale:
Closes s327-A4-g5v-03-03's signed ESCALATE per its own reopenCondition: "Reopen when a new figures.tsx component exists depicting two differently-proportioned rectangular solids compared side by side with equal volume highlighted; or if remedials[0].concept.body is ever authored to diverge from c2.body." A4's finding (reports/closure/S327_ASSESS_A4.md#g5v-03-03), re-verified by reading the lesson JSON directly before touching anything: neither c1 nor c2 carried a figure key, and this lesson's central claim -- that two differently-shaped/dimensioned solids can share the same volume -- was asserted only in feedback text (i1's successFeedback: "60 -- and B is also 60, so two different shapes hold the same volume"; i2's successFeedback: "both C and D have the same volume even though their dimensions differ"); the estimateSlider widgets themselves only ever ask the learner to find ONE of each pair's volume, never show the two solids side by side, and never have the learner verify the second solid independently. A4 checked every registered vm-* figure and found none depicting two differently-proportioned solids compared with equal volume highlighted. A4 also found and fixed an unrelated dangling-comparative language defect in k1/ch1/the remedial ("the taller solid" with no stated comparison partner) -- that fix is already landed in the lesson JSON and is unaffected by this record. Nothing about the math, remedials, or progression was otherwise defective per A4.

FIX: authored a new figures.tsx component, VmEqualVolumesCompare (registered as "vm-equal-volumes-compare"), depicting Solid A (base 20, 3 layers) as a wide, short stack and Solid B (base 12, 5 layers) as a narrower, taller stack, both resting on one shared ground line so their different proportions are the entire visual point, connected by an "=" sign, with a bottom caption stating the arithmetic directly: "20 x 3 = 12 x 5 = 60". Arithmetic verified: 20*3=60 and 12*5=60 -- confirmed correct and confirmed to be exactly i1's own already-authored pair (i1.widget.prompt: "Solid A is 20 by 3; solid B is 12 by 5", target 60), not an invented example; src/components/s328Figures.test.tsx asserts both the arithmetic and that these are i1's numbers (not i2's 14x4/7x8=56 pair) by loading the lesson JSON directly and checking i1.widget.prompt/target. Bound to c2 only, deliberately NOT c1: c2's own sentence ("Different shapes can hold identical volumes, which is exactly why the count settles the question and appearances do not") IS this exact claim, so binding there is a direct, truthful match; c1 ("compute both volumes and the larger count wins") precedes i1's own predict-before-reveal question ("A is 20x3 and B is 12x5. Which is larger? Equal -- both 60, or A") -- putting this lesson's real 20x3/12x5=60 pair on c1 would hand the learner that prediction's answer before they commit to it. By the time c2 renders (after c1, i1, and k1 have all already played), i1 has already completed and its own successFeedback has already stated "60 -- and B is also 60" in words -- so drawing that same, already-revealed pair at c2 adds the missing picture without previewing anything the learner has not already been told, and i2's own 14x4/7x8=56 pair (which the learner has NOT yet seen at c2's position in the lesson) is untouched by this figure and remains a fully independent second exercise. This asymmetric, deliberately-one-sided binding follows the exact precedent set in the S324 wave for pc-03-01/c2, which was left intentionally unfigured under a documented withheld-pin rationale (reports/closure/S324_ENGFIG.md, "c2 remains deliberately unfigured per the session271 withheld pin") rather than force-symmetric coverage. Also bound the same figure to remedials[0].concept (rem-g5v-compare-c), whose body is byte-identical to c2.body (the same non-gating S316 section-6 debt item A4 recorded and did not fix) -- since the figure already truthfully matches c2.body, it matches the remedial concept's identical text too, mirroring Worker D's best-in-batch remedial-figure pattern from S316_ADJUDICATION_REMEDIAL_STANDARD.md section 4.

visualDecision=SUFFICIENT (not merely PREFERRED): the lesson's central claim now has a correct, verified, numerically-exact static figure directly on the concept step that states it, PLUS genuine interactive coverage of the underlying computation via two estimateSlider widgets (i1, i2) that require the learner to actually compute and slide to each volume -- the same combination this same A4 assessor rated SUFFICIENT for g5v-01-01 in the same batch. decision=KEEP because A4 already confirmed the math (i1 60=20x3=12x5, i2 56=14x4=7x8, k2 216, k3 6), the remedial diagnostic-equivalence fix, and progression (k3's division step is a genuine reversal-of-operation transfer item) are all sound, and the sole blocking axis (visual) is now resolved. gradeLanguageDecision=FIT is carried forward unchanged from A4, including A4's own already-landed "taller solid" language fix -- no further text was touched by this record, only a figure key was added to two steps.
